title: Filter Users by Email Pattern Using REGEXP
description:
Find all users whose email address belongs to the `example.com` domain using a regular expression filter.

**Table: users** — `id`, `name`, `email`

Output columns: `name`, `email`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com'),(2,'Bob','bob@gmail.com'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com'),(4,'Dave','dave@yahoo.com'),(5,'Eve','eve@example.com'),(6,'Frank','frank@company.org'),(7,'Grace','grace@example.com'),(8,'Henry','henry@hotmail.com');
solution_sql: SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE regexp_matches(email, '.*@example\.com$') ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: 8 users; Alice, Carol, Eve, Grace have @example.com emails — 4 rows returned

hints: In DuckDB use regexp_matches(col, pattern) or col ~ 'pattern' to test a regular expression.
Escape the dot in the domain with \. to match a literal dot; without escaping, . would match any character.
explanation: The pattern .*@example\.com$ matches any string that ends with @example.com. The dot before com is escaped as \. to prevent it from matching any character. Alice, Carol, Eve, and Grace all match. Bob (gmail), Dave (yahoo), Frank (company.org), and Henry (hotmail) do not match — 4 rows returned.
